summary.tldr: Creates an Ombud for Citizenship and Immigration to review complaints, investigate unfair treatment, and report findings and recommendations.
what_it_does: Establishes the Office of the Ombud for the Department of Citizenship and Immigration, and sets seven-year terms, eligibility rules, pay, staff, and office location.
Gives the Ombud power to review department policies, programmes, training, and processing standards for fairness, bias, racism, and discrimination.
Allows any person to complain, and lets the Ombud investigate on their own, at the minister's request, or after a complaint.
Lets the Ombud summon witnesses, require documents and information, and make reports to the minister and complainants with findings and recommendations.
Requires the minister to respond to the Ombud's recommendations, publish annual and special reports, and comply with a parliamentary review every five years.
Amends the Language Skills Act and several other Acts to add the new office to federal lists and schedules.
summary.background: The bill says the Ombud would examine department practices to ensure they are fair, equitable, unbiased, non-racist and non-discriminatory, including systemic racism and systemic discrimination.
